title: After I insert the data, I do a search, and the search results are empty

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I'm using a go language client, and when I search for user_id on an inserted vector, I can't get anything.

The data volume of the whole collection is about 30 million, and the overall return time is about 7ms. I wonder if there is no search.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
If the search results are empty after inserting data, it's possible that there is an issue with the data or the search query.

Here are some things you can check:

Check if the data has been properly inserted: You can try retrieving a specific data point and verifying that the values are correct. You can also check if the number of data points in the collection matches the number of data points that you have inserted.

Check if the search query is correct: You can try running a simpler search query to see if it returns any results. For example, you can try searching for the nearest neighbors of a specific data point or searching for data points with a specific value. If the simpler search query returns results, then the issue may be with the original search query.

Check if the search parameters are correct: Make sure that the search parameters such as the number of nearest neighbors or the search radius are appropriate for your data and search query. If the search parameters are too restrictive, then it's possible that there are no results that match the search criteria.

Check if the distance metric is appropriate: Make sure that the distance metric that you are using is appropriate for your data and search query. If the distance metric is not appropriate, then the search results may not be accurate.

Check if the search index is properly built: If you are using a search index, make sure that it is properly built and optimized for your data and search query. You can try rebuilding the index or optimizing the index settings to see if it improves the search results.

If you are still unable to find the issue, you may need to provide more information about your data, search query, and the search index that you are using, so that we can provide more specific advice.
